versionLabel: Bocconi Online Test - Law (a.y. 2027-28 admissions cycle; booking window 13 July 2026 - 20 April 2027)
region: Italy (Università Bocconi, Milan). Taken remotely from anywhere; booking windows differ for "Italian applicants" vs "international applicants".
admissionsCycle: Academic year 2027-28 (Early Session: 2-29 September 2026; Winter Session: 25 November 2026 - 26 January 2027). Test attempts from earlier academic years cannot be reused for the 2027-28 selection.
deliveryMode: Fully online, taken from the candidate's own room on their own computer, via an external webtesting platform (bocconiwebtesting.giuntipsy.com, Giunti Psychometrics). Remote-proctored: audio and video recorded, front webcam plus a side-mounted mobile device running ProctorExam, screen sharing via a Chrome extension, and a Safe Exam Browser lockdown browser. Candidate books a calendar date and may start at any time from 12:00am to 11:59pm CET/CEST on that date. €60 per attempt. Test can be taken in Italian or English (language choice is independent of the programme's language of instruction).
summary: The Law programme does NOT use the same test as the other bachelor programmes: Bocconi publishes two distinct test types, the "Bocconi Online Test" and the "Bocconi Online Test - Law", which "differ in content" and are bought, booked and attempted separately (four attempts per test type per year). Both are 50 multiple-choice questions in 75 minutes, remote-proctored on the same platform, scored +1 / 0 / -0.2 (-0.33 for three-option critical-thinking items), with a 17/50 eligibility floor; but the Law blueprint is 5 Mathematics / 11 Reading comprehension / 6 Numerical reasoning / 18 Logic and critical thinking / 10 Verbal reasoning, versus 24 Mathematics / 11 / 6 / 9 for the standard test. The Law test is forward-only: questions are shown three per screen and, once "Next" is clicked, returning to a previous screen is impossible. Choosing the Bocconi Online Test - Law (or the LSAT) restricts the candidate to Law School programmes only; the test is one non-adaptive fixed form and counts for 55% of the admission ranking, with third-last and second-last year GPA counting 45%.
timingAndBreaks: Single continuous 75-minute session for all 50 questions. There is no published per-section time limit and no scheduled break; the candidate is not permitted to leave once the test has started. The test closes automatically when the allotted time expires and answers are saved and submitted. Time spent on proctoring "additional recordings"/checks requested by the platform mid-test is not counted against the test duration ("The time required to carry out the requested checks will not be counted as part of the test duration"). The online practice simulation Bocconi publishes is also 50 questions in 75 minutes "regulated by a timer", but Bocconi does not publish whether the live test shows an equivalent visible countdown. Approved accommodations for disabilities/SLD may include additional time, applied via a code entered at purchase; the amount of additional time is not published.
navigationAndReview: Strictly sequential, forward-only. Official rules: "The test presents 3 questions on each screen and you must proceed by following the order in which the questions are presented." and "By clicking the 'Next' button, you will move to the next screen and will not be able to return to previous screens." A "Test Navigation" panel is shown on every page as a guide. Questions may be left blank (omitted answers score 0 and the Italian page states each student decides autonomously which and how many questions to attempt), but a skipped question cannot be returned to once its screen is passed. There is no flag-for-review-and-return mechanism. Finishing: the candidate clicks "Finish", a summary page appears listing all questions "including both answered and omitted questions", then "Submit All and Finish" submits. Bocconi does not publish whether answers can still be changed from that summary page. Total score is displayed immediately at the end; a Test Score Report with per-subject-area scores and correct/wrong/omitted counts is available in the personal area within ~48 hours.
calculatorRules: No calculator of any kind. The Instructions and Rules of Conduct list among prohibited items "notebooks, notes, formula sheets, calculators or any sources/resources available online". The only permitted items on the desk are the computer, an identity document, 1 pencil/pen, 2 blank A4 sheets of paper, a beverage (glass, unlabeled bottle or reusable bottle) and the printed/written test credentials. No on-screen calculator is mentioned anywhere in the official test description or rules. Headphones/earbuds, second monitors, wireless mice/keyboards and any additional connected devices are also prohibited. The University may later compare the content of the scratch sheets against the activity recorded during the test.
adaptiveBehavior: Not adaptive. Bocconi describes a single fixed 75-minute form of 50 items with no routing, no modules and no stage-based difficulty adjustment. The English page states "The questions are distributed within the test in a mixed way both by difficulty level and by topic."; the Italian page says the same thing as "in modo casuale" (randomly). Either way, difficulty and topic are interleaved across the whole test rather than delivered as difficulty-targeted stages. A practical consequence: the five subject areas are NOT delivered as contiguous, separately timed blocks — items of different areas are mixed throughout, three per screen. Bocconi does not publish the item pool size, whether forms are randomised per candidate, or whether any items are unscored pretest items.
scoringRawRules: Raw scoring is published and deterministic: right answer +1 point; missing/omitted answer 0 points; wrong answer -0.2 points. Exception: "For questions of the 'critical thinking' area that give only three possible answer options, the penalty will be -0.33 points". Maximum raw score is therefore 50. There is an eligibility floor: "Applicants who receive a total score (penalties included) lower than 17 will not be considered in the selection process" (the Italian page phrases this as a "soglia minima generale di 17 su 50 punti"). The raw score is the reported score — there is NO raw-to-scaled conversion published for the Bocconi test itself. The 11/24 Mathematics sub-minimum applies only to the Bachelor in Mathematical and Computing Sciences for Artificial Intelligence, an Undergraduate School programme, and is therefore irrelevant to the Law test (which has only 5 Mathematics items and cannot be used to apply to that programme).
scoringScaleRules: No scaled score exists. The candidate receives the raw penalised total out of 50 plus per-subject-area subtotals and correct/wrong/omitted counts on the Test Score Report, plus a 10-character alphanumeric Reference Number identifying the attempt. For admission, the test score is weighted 55% and third-last/second-last year GPA 45%. Bocconi states that "SAT/ACT scores and Bocconi online test results are considered equivalent for evaluation purposes" using "an internal conversion system based on comparative tables that analyze candidate percentiles" — those tables are not published. Test-taker may hold up to four Bocconi Online Test - Law attempts per academic year and chooses which attempt to use; if multiple different tests are uploaded the portal "will pick the highest".
scoringNotPubliclyDocumented: The internal percentile-based conversion/comparative tables Bocconi uses to equate Bocconi Online Test - Law scores with SAT, ACT and LSAT scores — explicitly described as an 'internal conversion system' with no tables published.
How the 55% test-score weight is normalised or rescaled before being combined with the 45% GPA weight to produce the admission ranking.
The GPA conversion methodology beyond the statement that applicants list grades and use a calculator in the application portal to generate a GPA on a scale of ten.

Any admission cut-off or 'competitive' score for the Law or Global Law programmes. The only officially published threshold is the 17/50 eligibility floor (and LSAT 147/180, SAT 1040, ACT composite 19 for the alternative routes). No official cut-off exists — competitive-score figures circulating on prep sites are not Bocconi statements.
Item Response Theory parameters, item difficulty calibration, or any empirical difficulty labelling of items.
Whether any of the 50 items are unscored pretest/experimental items.
The item pool size and whether forms are randomised per candidate or per session.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief treats Bocconi as a single exam family, 'Bocconi Online Test — undergraduate and law', implying one test with two variants or one shared configuration.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: Bocconi publishes two separate, separately purchasable test types with different content blueprints and different downstream eligibility. Choosing the Law test locks the candidate out of all Undergraduate School programmes. Attempts are counted per test type (four each).
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Model bocconi-online-test-law as its own exam configuration with its own examKey, blueprint, question bank tags and taxonomy — not as a 'mode' flag on the undergraduate config. Do not share domain slugs between the two; the Mathematics domain in particular has a radically different weight (5 vs 24 items) and a much narrower syllabus.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief lists response types the engine must support including quantitative comparison, data sufficiency, numeric entry, multi-select and essay.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: None of these are needed for the Bocconi Online Test - Law. Every published item description is a multiple-choice item with one correct answer; reading comprehension items hang off shared passages. There is no writing/essay component anywhere in the Bocconi Law selection, and motivational writing is explicitly excluded from assessment.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: This exam config declares supportedResponseTypes = [single_select, passage_group] only. Do not surface numeric-entry or essay UI in this exam's practice or simulation players. The 'data propositions' item type is a single-select judgement item, NOT GMAT-style data sufficiency — tag it as a skill, not a response type.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief directs investigation of 'Bocconi navigation, penalties, eligibility thresholds, and program-specific requirements' as open questions.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: All four are now officially documented for the 2027-28 cycle: navigation is forward-only in 3-question screens; penalties are -0.2 (-0.33 for three-option critical-thinking items); the eligibility floor is 17/50; Law-specific requirements are the separate Law test, the 2-preference cap, the LSAT alternative at 147/180, and Italian-language instruction for the Law LMG/01 programme.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Bocconi Law can ship a genuinely exam-accurate simulation for timing, navigation lock, penalty scoring and the 17-point eligibility flag. Only option-count rendering needs a documented approximation disclaimer.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief asks about 'Claims presenting "competitive" admissions scores as official thresholds.'
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: Bocconi publishes exactly one Bocconi-test threshold (17/50) and it is an eligibility floor, not an admission cut-off. No admission cut-off score is published for Law or Global Law. Selection is a ranking on 55% test + 45% GPA against ~240 Law and ~80 Global Law places.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: The app must present 17 as 'minimum to be considered', never as 'the score you need'. Do not display any target score, admission probability, or 'competitive range' for Bocconi Law. Disable any score-goal feature for this exam.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief asks to investigate 'Outdated LSAT Analytical Reasoning / logic-games material.'
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: Bocconi's own SAT and ACT page — which is the official page documenting the LSAT route into Bocconi Law — still describes the LSAT as containing an 'Analytical Reasoning' section measuring the ability 'to understand a structure of relationships'. This description was not cross-checked against LSAC in this session, so the exact nature of the discrepancy is not confirmed here.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Do not source LSAT content specifications from Bocconi's page. Bocconi is authoritative only for the acceptance rule and the 147/180 minimum; the LSAT exam spec must come from LSAC (Agent A's LSAT workstream). Flag this so the two workstreams do not silently contradict each other on the public LSAT guide page.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief assumes exam configurations may need 'adaptive-practice policies' and warns against 'unsupported claims about proprietary adaptive scoring.'
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: The Bocconi Online Test - Law is explicitly non-adaptive: one fixed 75-minute form with difficulty and topic mixed throughout.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Set adaptive=false in this exam config and hide any adaptive-routing UI. Our own adaptive DRILL policy may still be used in practice mode, but it must be labelled 'our educational approximation' and must never be described as mirroring the real test.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: n/a — this is an internal inconsistency found between two official Bocconi pages, recorded per instruction 4.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: The English test page lists 'Reading comprehension : 11 questions' while the Italian page lists 'Comprensione del testo : 11 brani' (11 passages). The five Law areas sum to 50 only if the figure is 11 QUESTIONS (5+11+6+18+10=50), so the Italian 'brani' wording appears to be an error.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Configure 11 reading-comprehension QUESTIONS drawn from a smaller number of passages, since the arithmetic only closes that way. Record the discrepancy in the public exam-format guide rather than silently picking one reading; do not publish a passage count, because Bocconi does not state one.

briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: The English page says items are distributed 'in a mixed way' by difficulty and topic; the Italian page says 'in modo casuale' (randomly). 'Mixed' and 'random' are not the same claim about form assembly.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Our simulation should interleave areas and difficulties but must not claim to replicate Bocconi's assembly rule. Public copy should say 'items from all five areas are interleaved rather than grouped', which both pages support.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: n/a — third inconsistency, within a single official page.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: The Admissions page states in one place that applicants 'must have already taken a selection test (Bocconi online test/Bocconi online test - Law, SAT/LSAT or ACT)' and later, under 'How to apply', that they 'must have already taken a selection test (Bocconi online test, SAT or ACT)' — omitting the Law test and LSAT.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Treat the fuller enumeration (which is repeated twice and matches the SAT/ACT page and the test page) as correct. Our admissions guide should list all four Law-eligible routes and note that one paragraph on the official page is abbreviated, rather than propagating the omission.

implementationNotes: Timing: single server-authoritative deadline of 75 minutes for the whole 50-item attempt. No per-section timers, no breaks, no pause. On expiry, auto-submit and persist whatever is answered — this matches the official 'the test will automatically close when the allotted time expires' behaviour exactly, so it can be labelled exam-accurate.

Navigation lock: implement a forward-only paging mode with pageSize=3. Once a page is committed, its items become immutable for the attempt. There is no flag-and-return, no question navigator that allows jumping backwards, and no end-of-test review-and-edit. This is the single most distinctive behaviour of this exam and the engine must support 'forwardOnly' as a first-class navigation policy, not as a Bocconi-specific hack — the standard Bocconi Online Test shares it.

Review page: after the last screen, show a read-only summary listing answered vs omitted items, then require an explicit second confirmation ('Submit All and Finish'). Because Bocconi does not publish whether answers are editable from that summary, render it read-only and label that choice as our conservative interpretation.

Scoring: raw scoring function is sum(+1 correct, 0 omitted, -0.2 wrong), with a per-item penaltyOverride of -0.33 for items flagged optionCount=3 in the critical-thinking/logic domain. Store the penalty as item-level config so the -0.2/-0.33 split is data, not code. Report the penalised total out of 50 and per-domain subtotals, mirroring the official score report.

Eligibility flag, not a grade: surface 'below 17 — would not be considered in Bocconi's selection' as a neutral eligibility indicator on results. Never render it as pass/fail, a target score, or an admission prediction.

No scaled score: do not compute or display any scaled score, percentile, or SAT/ACT/LSAT equivalent for this exam. Bocconi's equating tables are internal and unpublished; producing a conversion would fabricate official equivalence. The results screen shows raw score, per-domain accuracy, timing and omission rate only.

Calculator: calculatorPolicy = 'none' for all five sections. Do not render an on-screen calculator in the simulation player. Optionally show a 'scratch paper only' notice, matching the 2 blank A4 sheets Bocconi permits.

Adaptive: adaptive=false. Pin the attempt to one immutable fixed form of 50 items assembled to the 5/11/6/18/10 blueprint, with areas interleaved rather than blocked. Persist the generated item order at attempt creation so a refresh cannot regenerate the form.

Response types: enable only single_select and passage_group for this exam. Reading comprehension items must be modelled as a passage group where several items share one stimulus; because paging is 3 items per screen and Bocconi does not document passage-to-screen mapping, keep a passage group intact within a page where possible and re-render the passage on every page that carries its items.

Option count: Bocconi publishes an option count only for some three-option critical-thinking items. Make optionCount a per-item authored field, default to 5 for our original items, and add a visible content-guide note that our option counts are our editorial choice, not a verified reproduction. Do not let the simulation claim option-count fidelity.

Language: the exam config needs a testLanguage dimension (it/en) that is independent of programme language. If we later localise, Bocconi Law content should exist in both Italian and English, and the public guide must state that the test language choice does not affect which programme you can apply to.

Accommodations: support an additionalTimeMultiplier hook but leave it unset/disabled for this exam, since Bocconi does not publish the amount of extra time granted. Do not offer a preset '+25%' or similar.

Domain weighting for study plans: the Law blueprint is logic-dominant (Logic and critical thinking 18 + Verbal reasoning 10 = 28 of 50, i.e. 56%) with Mathematics at only 5 items on a narrow syllabus (plane geometry, analytic geometry of points and lines, sets, real-number ordering, percentages, unit conversion). Study-plan weighting and diagnostic blueprint must follow this, and must NOT reuse the undergraduate test's maths-heavy weighting.

Separation of admissions content: the Law hub must not inherit undergraduate copy. Specifically, the 11/24 Mathematics sub-minimum and the Mathematical and Computing Sciences programme are Undergraduate School only and must be excluded from all Law pages. Conversely, the LSAT route, the 147/180 LSAT minimum and the 2-preference cap are Law-only.

Public guide accuracy guardrails: state the admissions cycle (2027-28) next to every claim; present 17/50 as an eligibility floor; do not publish any competitive or target score; and do not source LSAT exam structure from Bocconi's page, which still describes an Analytical Reasoning section.

Practice vs simulation labelling: Bocconi runs its own free official simulation (50 questions / 75 minutes, no proctoring, with post-test review). Our simulation differs in that it will allow review of all items afterwards; label that clearly as our educational addition, and keep the in-test forward-only lock faithful.
